link.host_enable: Let paired machines connect to this one
link.host_hint: Off by default. When on, this machine listens for connections from machines you have paired with, and your firewall will ask once.
link.portmap_mapped: Your router opened the port automatically ({via}). Invites now carry {address}, so this machine is reachable from another network.
link.portmap_unsupported: Your router did not answer automatic port opening (UPnP / NAT-PMP). Connections from this network still work. From elsewhere, use the IPv6 address above, an overlay network, or turn UPnP on in the router.
link.portmap_carrier: Your router opened the port, but your ISP puts it behind carrier-grade NAT — the address behind it is not reachable from the internet. Use the IPv6 address above, or an overlay network.
link.portmap_failed: Your router refused to open the port: {detail}
link.create_code_hint: One code, valid for five minutes, usable once. It carries this machine’s address and identity, so nothing has to be typed on the other side.
link.paste_on_other: Copy this and paste it on the other machine.
link.no_devices: No machine has been paired with this one yet.
link.no_machines: No other machines yet. Create a code on the machine you want to reach, then paste it here.
link.clipboard_found: Found a connection code for {name} in your clipboard.
link.err_unreachable: Nothing answered at {addresses}. The machine may be asleep, on another network, or blocked by its firewall.
link.err_tls: Something answered, but the two DevDecks could not agree on how to talk. Check that both are up to date.
link.err_fingerprint: The machine that answered is not the one you paired with. This is either a different machine at that address, or someone in the middle. Nothing was sent to it.
link.err_unpaired: That machine no longer allows this one in. Create a new code on it.
link.err_expired: That code has expired. Codes last five minutes — create a new one on the other machine.
link.err_version: The two machines are running different DevDeck versions. Update both.
link.err_not_a_code: That is not a connection code. Copy the whole line, starting with DDLINK1.
link.err_truncated: That code looks cut off. Copy the whole line and paste it again.
link.err_malformed: That code could not be read. Create a new one on the other machine.
cockpit.restore_machine_offline: Cannot restore “{name}” — {machine} is not reachable. It stays saved.
cockpit.remote_file_unavailable: That file is on {machine}, not on this computer.
cockpit.remote_image_unsupported: Pasting an image into a session on another machine is not supported yet.
proj.remote_local_only: That folder is on {machine}. This action only works on projects on this computer.
cockpit.remote_image_too_large: That image is too large to send to another machine (5 MB limit).
cockpit.remote_image_failed: Could not send the image to the other machine — nothing was pasted.
cockpit.adopted_remote: Picked up {n} session(s) already running on {machine}.
diag.title: Diagnostics log
link.err_unreachable_head: None of this machine's addresses answered:
link.dial_refused: connection refused (the machine is up, nothing listening there)
link.dial_timed-out: no answer (the route exists; the packets went nowhere)
link.dial_tls: connected, but the two ends could not agree on security
link.advice_no-ipv6-here: The only addresses reachable from another network are IPv6, and this machine has no IPv6 route. No setting on the other machine can fix that — this one needs a network with IPv6, or an overlay such as Tailscale at both ends.
link.advice_far-side-blocking: There IS a route to the IPv6 address and nothing answered on it. The other machine's router is blocking inbound connections, or that machine is asleep.
link.advice_same-network-only: Every address offered only works inside that machine's own network. It had no address to give that reaches it from outside.
